title: Circumbinary Disks of the Protostellar Binary Systems in the L1551 Region
question: What are the structures, gas motions and temperatures of the circumbinary and circumstellar disks of the protobinary L1551 IRS 5, and how do they compare with L1551 NE and with hydrodynamical simulations?

what.value: 1.3-mm continuum image of L1551 IRS 5 used for spectral index

evidence.quote: deduced from the present 0.9-mm and the published 1.3-mm data (cite: cru19)

external_data.citation: Cruz-Sáenz de Miera et al. 2019 (cite: cru19)

what.value: VLA 7-mm relative positions of binary in 2012

evidence.quote: As compared to the relative position derived from the VLA 7-mm observations of L1551 IRS 5 made in 2012 (cite: lim16a)
a factor of 3 higher than the canonical value of 1.7 $\times$ 10$^{-7}$ (cite: cra04)

recipe.method: Continuum from line-free channels with uniform weighting and multiscale clean, phase self-cal (120 s); lines with natural weighting and multiscale clean after continuum subtraction

recipe.goal: Source positions, sizes and brightness temperatures
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fits for centroids and deconvolved sizes; Rayleigh-Jeans conversion to T_B
assumptions: Disk PA 160 deg, inclination 60 deg, coplanar CBD and CSDs

recipe.goal: Spectral index map and CBD mass
recipe.method: Alpha from 0.9 and 1.3 mm maps convolved to common beam, pixels >10 sigma; mass M=S d^2/(kappa B(T))
assumptions: gas-to-dust 100; kappa_250um=0.1 cm2/g, beta=1.0 giving kappa_0.9mm=0.028; d=140 pc

recipe.goal: Kinematics from channel maps, P-V diagrams and peak T_B maps
recipe.method: Velocity channel maps, P-V cuts along major (PA 160) and minor (PA 70) axes with Keplerian curves, peak brightness temperature maps (moment 8)
SFUMATO isothermal simulation (T=100 K) tailored to IRS 5, LTE radiative transfer with fitted T(r) and C18O abundance, CASA observing simulation, same imaging
key_parameters: X(C18O)=5.1e-7; T(r)=max[62 K (r_N/100au)^-0.5, 48 K (r_S/100au)^-0.5]; snapshot at 58.7 orbital periods

evidence.quote: The peak brightness temperature toward Source N exceeds $\gtrsim$260 K and that toward Source S $\gtrsim$160 K.
The peak brightness temperature toward Source N exceeds $\gtrsim$260 K and that toward Source S $\gtrsim$160 K.

answer_key.quantity: Relative position of S wrt N (2017)

evidence.quote: the relative position of Source S with respect to Source N (dRA, dDec) = (0.057$''$,-0.363$''$) is adopted
The outermost extent of the CBD is $\sim$150 au
The $\alpha$ value in the CBD is $\sim$3.0 - 3.7, while that in the CSDs is as low as $\sim$2.

answer_key.quantity: Peak molecular-line T_B (C18O, 13CO, CS, SO, OCS)

evidence.quote: The peak values in the C$^{18}$O, $^{13}$CO, CS, SO, and OCS maps are 78, 92, 88, 106, and 86 K

answer_key.quantity: Fitted temperature profile normalizations at 100 au
LOS velocities of Source N and S

evidence.quote: $V_{LSR}$ = 6.85 km s$^{-1}$ and 5.95 km s$^{-1}$, respectively

not_stated_but_needed: Line-free channel ranges for continuum and continuum subtraction
Self-calibration reference/model details and which antennas/spws
Spectral index map method details (regridding, alignment of 1.3 mm proper motion shift)
Simulation initial conditions, snapshot choice details, CASA simulobserve weather parameters
Continuum flux extraction region for CBD (1.40 Jy)
Velocity channel width used for maps
missing_for_reproduction: Simulation setup and outputs (in Matsumoto et al. 2019)
1.3-mm data from Cruz-Saenz de Miera et al. 2019
score_reason: Imaging recipe fairly well given and data public, but simulation and several clean/channel details are deferred or missing.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, imaging parameters mostly stated, and key results (T_B, sizes, spectral index, CBD mass) are numeric; simulation part is not reproducible from this paper alone.
